text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 2141240000 - Multiple TLS handshake failures observed from hosted-api-eu. Severity: P2. Paging on-call.

emma_oncall: acked. I'm pulling logs for eu-region gateways now. any customer-facing impact?

alex_support: getting a couple of reports: customers seeing 502s and 'TLS handshake timeout' from our SDKs; one support ticket from ACME Corp with elevated errors around 21:06 UTC.

emma_oncall: confirmed spike in 502/525 on the EU edge. Router metrics show increased TLS errors on gw-eu-2 and gw-eu-4. Adding maia to help with mitigation.

maia_sre: on it. can someone paste the top-level error we see on the gateway?

jonah_prod: here's a sample from gw-eu-2 syslog at 21:06:12:

```
2026-03-14T21:06:12Z gw-eu-2 tls: handshake failed: remote error: tls: handshake failure (alert 40)
2026-03-14T21:06:12Z gw-eu-2 conn: client 10.10.2.45:52344 -> backend 10.20.5.11:443: tls handshake err
```

maia_sre: interesting, alert 40 = handshake failure, could be cert mismatch or TLS version/protocol problem. raj, can you check VPC peering and any recent network changes?

raj_net: I'm seeing intermittent ICMP fragmentation issues on the peering route between vpc-eu-edge and vpc-backend. MTU counters spiking on peering-gw-1 around the same time window. Running quick check: `ip -s link show peer0` shows TX dropped due to oversized packets.

emma_oncall: that would explain fragmented TLS ClientHello packets being dropped -> handshake fails. Any recent cert rotations?

jonah_prod: we rotated CA cert on backends an hour before the incident window as part of scheduled rotation. No config changes to TLS cipher suites.

maia_sre: hypothesis v1: cert rotation + MTU fragmentation = handshake failure when clients send larger ClientHello (SNI + ALPN + early data). Hypothesis v2: peering path MTU reduced by a network config change leading to fragmentation and routers dropping fragments (df bit). Let's collect pcap from gw-eu-2 and gw-eu-4 and run openssl s_client from within the edge to backend.

emma_oncall: capturing pcap now on gw-eu-2 (filter host 10.20.5.11): `tcpdump -w /tmp/tls-hs-gw-eu-2.pcap host 10.20.5.11 and port 443`

raj_net: concurrently checking peering appliance logs. I can already see an automated MTU adjustment ran at 21:05:47 due to path change from our cloud provider. That correlates well.

alex_support: ACME gave a curl sample showing handshake fail:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
*   Trying 52.207.11.45...
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (52.207.11.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, server accepted to use http/1.1
* TLS handshake error
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

maia_sre: opened the pcap. I see fragmented TLS ClientHello (large extension list). Several fragments never reassembled; peers respond with RST after timeout. tcpdump snippet:

```
21:06:12.123456 IP 10.10.2.45.52344 > 10.20.5.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 123:456, ack 1, win 64240, length 333
21:06:12.123457 IP (frag 1/2) ...
21:06:12.123458 IP (frag 2/2) ...
```

maia_sre: fragments look like DF=0? hmm. but router logs show dropping of fragments due to above-MTU size on peering.

raj_net: confirmed: cloud peering device changed PMTU to 1400 at 21:05:47, while our edge expects 1500. Packets >1400 are being fragmented; our infra doesn't reassemble fragments at the TLS termination stage (we rely on kernel offload). That causes incomplete handshake data to reach the TLS stack.

emma_oncall: mitigation options: 1) roll back the CA rotation to rule out cert mismatch (fast but risk to infra config), 2) force MSS/MTU adjustment on edge hosts to 1400 to avoid fragmentation, 3) implement temporary TCP MSS clamping on peering routers, 4) enable TLS passthrough to backend (bad for observability). Thoughts?

maia_sre: prefer MSS clamping at peering or host MTU change — lowest blast radius. I'll coordinate with raj to push clamping rule. If that doesn't reduce errors within 5 min, we can consider rolling back rotation.

raj_net: applying MSS clamp at peering-gw-1 now: `iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360` (pushing via config manager).

emma_oncall: pushed to canary peering node gw-1. watch metrics.

(2 minutes later)

maia_sre: metrics update: TLS handshake error rate on gw-eu-2 dropped from 18% -> 2% within 90s of clamping. gw-eu-4 showing similar improvement after replicate.

alex_support: ACME confirms latency/errors returning to normal. They reported success reconnect at 21:08:50. :thumbsup:

jonah_prod: good. we'll keep mitigation in place while we finish RCA. No rollback required.

emma_oncall: building timeline for RCA: will paste initial timeline here and ask folks to annotate.

- 21:04:03 UTC: scheduled CA rotation started (backend fleet)
- 21:05:47 UTC: cloud provider automatic PMTU adjustment observed on peering route
- 21:06:12 UTC: first TLS handshake failures spike reported by gateways
- 21:07:00 UTC: on-call paged; pcap captures started
- 21:07:30 UTC: MSS clamping pushed to peering-gw-1 (canary)
- 21:08:10 UTC: errors decline on canary gw
- 21:08:50 UTC: customers report recovery

maia_sre: adding hypotheses notes:
- H1: combination of new CA rotation increased ClientHello size (new OCSP stapling/extension?) leading to packets exceeding the new PMTU -> fragmentation -> dropped fragments -> handshake fails.
- H2: PMTU change alone would affect large ClientHellos regardless of cert change; rotation just coincidentally occurred.
- H3: a misconfigured middlebox started dropping fragments with DF mismatch.

raj_net: data points for H1: pcap shows larger TLS ext length post-rotation (SCT / OCSP staples present). H2 data: cloud logs show path change that reduced PMTU. H3: peering appliance config shows default drop on fragmented packets for performance reasons.

jonah_prod: action items (assigned):
- maia_sre: write incident notes + gather pcap, openssl s_client outputs, and sample client traces. (ETA 60m)
- raj_net: coordinate with cloud provider to explain PMTU change and ensure peering nodes preserve original MTU; request a persistent MSS clamp if needed. (ETA 30m)
- emma_oncall: notify customer-facing teams and add ACME ticket note that we mitigated. (ETA 10m)
- jonah_prod: review CA rotation payload size and see if we can reduce extensions or stagger rotation. (ETA 2h)

maia_sre: quick reproducible check — from gw-eu-2 run:

```
# from edge to backend
openssl s_client -connect 10.20.5.11:443 -debug -msg
CONNECTED(00000003)
>>> TLS 1.2 Handshake [length 0139], ClientHello
<<< no response (incomplete ClientHello fragments)
```

maia_sre: after MSS clamp applied, same command completes and shows server Hello.

emma_oncall: escalation/communication: I'm creating an incident summary for customers: short explanation + mitigation + next steps. Will flag for postmortem.

alex_support: adding ACME ticket update: "We observed intermittent TLS handshake failures between 21:06-21:09 UTC due to a network MTU mismatch on the peering path. We applied a temporary MSS clamp and verified recovery. We're doing a full RCA."

maia_sre: final notes for in-thread RCA tracking: keep hypotheses open until we collect provider's response and full pcap analysis. We'll check if new CA payload can be reduced in size or rotations staged to avoid simultaneous large hello sizes. Also verify our edge reassembly behavior and kernel offload expectations.

emma_oncall: thanks all — keeping channel for follow-ups. If anything new pops up, ping `@emma_oncall` directly.

incident-bot: Incident 2141240000 moved to "mitigated" at 2141240365. Postmortem requested: /incidents/postmortem-requests
